extracted.intended_audience: machine learning researchers submitting to or reviewing for TMLR (authors, reviewers, editors)
extracted.subtask_description: High-level rules and expectations for submitting and reviewing manuscripts for Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), including evaluation emphasis, originality requirements, review process, format and media support, and procedural timelines. Geared toward authors preparing submissions and reviewers/editors evaluating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on technical correctness over subjective significance
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR emphasizes technical correctness over subjective significance, to ensure scientific discourse on topics that may not yet be accepted in mainstream venues but may be important in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should prioritize correctness, rigor, and soundness of methods and results rather than subjective judgments about the perceived novelty or impact. This encourages publication of technically correct work even if its immediate significance is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / no overlap with previously published work
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR does not accept submissions that have any overlap with previously published work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure submissions are original and do not overlap with prior publications. The policy implies that previously published material or substantial overlap will lead to rejection; clarify and avoid dual submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prepare submissions consistent with double-blind review expectations (e.g., anonymization where appropriate). Reviewers and editors will follow double-blind procedures during evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness and transparency via OpenReview
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR maximizes openness and transparency by hosting the review process on OpenReview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review process (and associated discussions) will be public/transparent on OpenReview, enabling readers and participants to view reviews and discourse. Authors and reviewers should expect public-facing interactions and follow OpenReview norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rolling submission and shortened review periods
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR employs a rolling submission process, shortened review period, and flexible timelines to enable fast turnarounds and deep interactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can submit at any time and should expect faster decisions compared to some other venues. The process is designed to enable ongoing interactions among authors, reviewers, and editors, so timely responses and engagement may be expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable manuscript length and support for shorter conference-style formats
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR caters to the shorter format manuscripts that are usually submitted to conferences and supports variable manuscript length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may submit shorter-format manuscripts typical of conference submissions; there is flexibility in manuscript length rather than a strict long-journal format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for interactive figures and videos (TMLR Beyond PDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR Beyond PDF is an HTML-based submission format that supports interactive figures and videos, along with usual LaTeX and images. TMLR papers can also have videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may use the Beyond PDF format to include interactive elements and videos in submissions; consider including such media when it aids clarity or demonstration. Check guidelines for format-specific submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: High level of quality and rigor for published articles
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR aims for a high level of quality and rigor for every published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should demonstrate rigorous methodology, clear exposition, reproducibility where applicable, and sufficient validation to meet the journal's quality expectations.
